new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Nixtamalized corn flour (Maseca and store equivalents), its own SKU in the Hispanic-foods aisle. It is not corn flour proper, not cornmeal, not corn starch and not any flour id: the lime treatment changes the food, the price and the use, and the board reports no commodity and no capture match while no vocabulary row shares a core word with it. Nothing on the board prices a nixtamalized corn product under another spelling, so this is a genuinely new food rather than a rename.

registrar_rulings.reason: No id in any namespace prices nixtamalized corn flour: the estate's only 'masa'/'harina' strings are EXCLUDE patterns inside hominy (commodities.json:42783-84) and cornmeal (:67319), meaning both corn neighbors deliberately fence masa harina out rather than carry it; the recipe-board baseline and recipe-commodities have no masa/harina/nixtamal row, the live feed has no price cell for it, and the only word-overlap hit (garam-masala, $0.9943/oz) is an unrelated spice. Nixtamalization makes it a different purchase from cornmeal and cornstarch (same-food-different-form vs cornmeal, different food vs cornstarch). Mint as recipe-only: add to recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json via add-commodity-rule.ps1 with include ['masa\s*harina','\bmaseca\b','instant\s+corn\s+masa'] and cornmeal-grade excludes (~150 patterns; explicitly exclude '\bcornmeal\b','polenta','grits?','corn\s*starch','tortillas?','tamales?','pupusa','arepa','masarepa','chips?','prepared','mix\b' plus the standard non-food block), and add commodity-dupe-allowlist.json pairs masa-harina<->cornmeal ('nixtamalized vs plain corn grind, different product/aisle/price') and masa-harina<->hominy ('same nixtamal process, whole canned kernel vs dry flour') so the daily audit never re-flags them. Vocabulary is a separate act: 'masa harina' also needs its own ingredients.json row (none shares a core word) with a label transcription for macros - fdc:169694/169696 are plausible SR Legacy matches but identity, not just macro agreement, must be confirmed before either is adopted.

macro_cross_check: Source published 613 cal / 40 protein for 6 servings. Recomputed over the 16 costed lines at source basis: 4218 cal and 258 g protein total, i.e. 703 cal and 43.1 g protein per serving. Protein is +7.7% against the source and calories +14.7%, both inside the band and both explained by the same two things: the beans are carried at the settled 425.2 g gross-can basis rather than drained solids, and the source's own figure almost certainly excludes the sour cream and cheddar toppings that I weighed. 703 cal sits inside the run band of 450-800 but nearer the ceiling than the other two, which is the reason the unquantified chips were dropped rather than given a nominal weight.
